objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with changes in behavior and memory over the past few months.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I've been having some changes lately—people tell me I’ve been acting inappropriately, laughing or saying things I shouldn’t, and sometimes I grab at them without meaning to. My memory has also gotten worse, and it’s harder for me to manage my personal needs and find the right words.

When did these behavior and memory/language changes start, and have they been gradually worsening or did they come on suddenly?
When did these behavior and memory/language changes start, and have they been gradually worsening or did they come on suddenly?
They started a few months ago and have been gradually getting worse. It’s not like a sudden change; my behavior and memory seem to decline steadily.
Have you had any weakness, numbness, trouble walking, balance problems, headaches, seizures, or episodes of confusion?

“No, I haven’t had weakness or numbness, and I’m not having trouble walking or balance problems. I haven’t had headaches, seizures, or any episodes of confusion beyond the memory and word-finding difficulties. ”
Have you noticed changes in your personality or social behavior before the memory problems—such as loss of empathy, poor judgment, disinhibition, compulsive behaviors, overeating, or apathy?

“Yes, my spouse says my judgment has been off and I don’t seem as aware of my actions with other people—I’ve been more disinhibited, sometimes inappropriate with laughter and foul language, and occasionally I touch or grab people without warning. It really seems tied to that earlier personality/social change, and then the memory trouble followed and has been worsening.”
Have you had any visual hallucinations, vivid dreams acting out in sleep, or fluctuations where cognition is much better some times and much worse at others?

“No, I don’t have visual hallucinations or anything like acting out in my sleep. I also haven’t noticed big day-to-day swings—my thinking feels steadily worse rather than much better some times and worse other times.”
Any tremor, stiffness, slowness of movement, or shuffling gait?

“No, I haven’t noticed tremors, stiffness, or slowed movement, and my walking and posture haven’t changed like a shuffling gait. I’m mainly dealing with the behavior changes first, then the memory and word-finding getting worse steadily.”
Any history of heavy alcohol use, head trauma, stroke, HIV/syphilis risk, or family history of early dementia or similar personality/language problems?

“No—there’s no heavy alcohol use, no head trauma, and no history of stroke. I’m not aware of any HIV or syphilis risk, and there isn’t a known family history of early dementia or similar personality or language problems.”
[DDX] behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia, Alzheimer disease, frontal lobe brain tumor, Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, vascular dementia
